scope: All ten standard overview videos in the current Understand AI section: about 36 minutes 49 seconds. The separate AI Brain Break debunking activity inside Layers is outside this overview-video audit.
method: Decoded each complete source sequentially and checked frame counts; visually inspected all 23 contact sheets sampled every six seconds, plus seven one-second detail sequences. Read fresh timestamped transcripts for all ten videos, current lesson teaching context, and the relevant retained repair/build records. These are frame-and-transcript findings, not a continuous audiovisual viewing or a new narration verdict. Automated transcript cues may contain recognition errors.
recommendation: Build three small photographic inserts: choosing helpful training feedback, assigning drink ratings, and revealing only the first coin. These make specific learning actions visible in about 28 seconds of supporting imagery. Keep the other seven videos as they are.

opportunities.title: Show someone choosing the more helpful answer
opportunities.cue: Next, the model learns from feedback about which answers people find more helpful.
opportunities.current: A seated, thinking student surrounded by chemistry, code, and essay icons. It shows subjects AI can help with, but not the feedback the narration is introducing.
opportunities.proposal: A photographic over-the-shoulder view of a person comparing two short answers to the same basketball question. A clearly labeled training-feedback panel makes the choice visible. Keep the readable answer fragments beside the photograph, rather than small on a distant laptop.
opportunities.benefit: Gives “feedback” a concrete meaning: a person compares answers and chooses the more useful one. It prepares learners for the preference-tuning board that follows.
beats: Compare: two short basketball answers, A and B.
Choose: highlight the answer with an actionable first step.
opportunities.treatment: About seven seconds. Use two states with one clear selection. Suggested answer fragments: A “Use good technique.” B “Start close to the hoop.” Label the demonstration “Training feedback.” Show a human preference, not an instant model improvement or an ordinary chat updating weights. Render all text separately for legibility. Narration and total duration stay unchanged.
opportunities.board: Keep the complete instruction-tuning and preference-tuning boards, their text, highlights, and camera moves. End the insert before the preference-tuning board appears.
opportunities.success: A learner can identify the comparison and selected answer before the board returns, without confusing training feedback with a normal chat.

opportunities.title: Turn drink characteristics into visible ratings
opportunities.cue: Imagine we’re running a simple taste test. We rate Coke and coffee across six characteristics: Sweet, Bitter, Fizz, Heat, Caffeine, and Dark, using a scale from zero for low to ten for high.
opportunities.current: A paper-style “Taste Test” graphic names Coke, coffee, six characteristics, and a 0–10 scale. The ingredients of the analogy are present, but nobody is shown assigning a rating.
opportunities.proposal: Two believable students compare Coke and coffee at a table, with the drinks clearly identified and a rating sheet in view. Pair the photograph with a clean six-position strip labeled Sweet, Bitter, Fizz, Heat, Caffeine, and Dark. Show a hand recording one illustrative rating, then guide attention along the six traits as they are named.
opportunities.benefit: Makes the bridge from a real characteristic to a number tangible. An ordered set of ratings then leads naturally into the existing numerical-profile board and mystery-drink quiz.
beats: Establish: the two drinks and a student rating sheet.
Record: one illustrative rating, such as Coke → Sweet → 9.
Connect: six consistently ordered traits and the 0–10 scale.
opportunities.treatment: About fifteen seconds. Keep one stable photographic setting and add restrained, narration-timed labels. Ratings are the lesson’s illustrative choices, not laboratory measurements. Do not imply caffeine is measured by tasting. Keep all six labels in the lesson’s order and make the 0-low/10-high scale readable. Do not reveal the later mystery-drink answer early. Preserve the later explanation that AI learns embedding values during training.
opportunities.board: Replace only the supporting taste-test graphic. Preserve the existing Coke/coffee table, hidden-label quiz and reveal, Coke/Pepsi comparison, seventh-dimension demonstration, taste-versus-AI comparison, and embedding-table lookup.
opportunities.success: A learner can explain how a characteristic receives a score and how each position keeps the same meaning. The photograph must not crowd the labels or make the analogy look like the actual AI training process.

opportunities.title: Reveal the first coin; keep the second unknown
opportunities.cue: We run the two-coin toss again, but this time someone peeks. They tell you the first coin landed on heads.
opportunities.current: A drawing of two hands and two coins. Both coin faces are partly visible, so the distinction between the known first result and the unknown second result is less explicit than it could be.
opportunities.proposal: A photographic tabletop demonstration with two coins already at rest under covers, labeled FIRST and SECOND. A hand lifts only the first cover to reveal heads. The second coin stays completely covered. Use a clear “First: heads” label while leaving “Second: unknown” visible.
opportunities.benefit: Shows exactly what the new evidence tells us—and what it does not. That makes the following reduction from four possible outcomes to two easier to understand.
beats: Before the clue: both results are covered.
New evidence: first coin is heads; second stays hidden.
opportunities.treatment: About six seconds. Use one fixed camera and two matching states, with a simple reveal on the spoken clue. Do not toss again, move or flip either coin during the reveal, show the second result, or calculate the answer on this shot. Composite precise labels separately. Confirm the short window is comfortable in the encoded excerpt.
opportunities.board: Keep all four-outcome diagrams, elimination animation, 25%→50% calculations, and the explanation that information changed, not the coins. Preserve the opening company imagery and all previously retained material outside this small supporting shot.
opportunities.success: A learner sees that only the first result becomes known. The photograph must make uncertainty clearer than the current drawing without rushing the next diagram.

lessons.title: Understand AI — Opener
lessons.reason: The car/under-the-hood analogy and section roadmap already orient the learner. A new detailed “good answer / bad answer” example would add reading and a second story before the section begins. Preserve the repaired words → tokens → vectors sequence.

lessons.title: Training
lessons.reason: Make human preference feedback visible. Keep the basketball practice analogy, shot/error demonstration, guess/check/adjust loop, all three training-phase boards, and the distinction between training and ordinary chat. No broad basketball restyling.

lessons.title: AI Is Math
lessons.reason: Clarify exactly which coin is known. Preserve the sample-space counting, outcome elimination, conditional-probability calculations, next-token example, and existing opening imagery.

lessons.title: Tokens
lessons.reason: The current demonstrations already show reusable text pieces, token IDs, and the return to readable words. Preserve the recently repaired examples, complete cards, and address analogy; a person at a laptop would not explain these operations better.

lessons.title: Embeddings
lessons.reason: Connect objects to assigned ratings. Preserve the existing student-ID photograph, mystery-drink quiz, Coke/Pepsi seventh dimension, analogy limits, and embedding-table lookup.

lessons.title: Transformer
lessons.reason: Context examples, CAT/IT connections, changing-number graphics, and word-order demonstrations carry the explanation. Keep the existing photographic examples. A new sarcasm scene would need extra context in a brief list of concepts; defer it.

lessons.title: Layers
lessons.reason: The horse-sentence example, neural-network diagram, changing number rows, CAT/IT progression, and depth-versus-computing-cost comparison explain cumulative processing. Preserve the recently repaired motion and readable values.

lessons.title: Vector Space
lessons.reason: The current city and drink maps, guided mystery-point comparisons, and movement of IT near CAT make abstract relationships visible. Retain the recent guided rebuild; a photographic cutaway would interrupt it.

lessons.title: How AI Answers
lessons.reason: The final-token handoff and guided probability/selection/reply sequence show the generation loop directly. Keep the current rebuild, first-word explanation, and stopping-token distinction.

lessons.title: One More Thing
lessons.reason: Unchanged probabilities with different picks, the 100-trial illustration, temperature distributions, and calculation-scale board teach the mechanism. Preserve these; an AI-chat photograph would hide the comparison.
